nodes.summary: Once a power of an ergodic chain is all-positive, every later power is all-positive: there is a threshold `w` past which every power is all-positive.
nodes.title: Powers of an ergodic chain are eventually all positive

nodes.summary: An ergodic chain has, for every pair of states, some positive power with a positive `(i, j)`-entry. (This is the per-pair form; it is strictly weaker than ergodicity, which asks for one power working for all pairs at once.)
nodes.title: Pairwise positive powers of an ergodic chain

nodes.summary: The convergence theorem (Levin, Peres and Wilmer, Theorem 4.9): a primitive (irreducible and aperiodic) stochastic matrix with stationary distribution `π` converges to `π` geometrically fast in total variation, uniformly in the starting state.
nodes.title: The convergence theorem

nodes.summary: The identity chain: `prob i j` is `1` on the diagonal and `0` elsewhere.
nodes.title: Identity Markov chain

nodes.summary: Ergodicity is exactly primitivity of the transition matrix. This is the bridge to Mathlib: `Matrix.IsPrimitive` is the same condition for a bare matrix, while `IsErgodic` is the stochastic-matrix form, with nonnegativity supplied by the `StochasticMatrix` structure.
nodes.title: Ergodicity is primitivity of the transition matrix

nodes.summary: The uniform chain is ergodic, with witness `n = 1`.
nodes.title: The uniform Markov chain is ergodic

nodes.summary: A finite-state Markov chain (given by its stochastic transition matrix `P`) is *ergodic* if some positive power `P^n` has all strictly positive entries.
nodes.title: Ergodic finite Markov chain

nodes.summary: Powers add: `matPow (a + b)` is the matrix product of `matPow a` and `matPow b`.
nodes.title: Additivity of recursive matrix powers

nodes.summary: The recursively defined power `matPow` agrees with the ordinary matrix power.
nodes.title: Recursive matrix power agrees with the matrix power

nodes.summary: Every power of the identity chain is the identity matrix.
nodes.title: Powers of the identity chain are the identity matrix

nodes.summary: One step of the power recursion: `matPow 1` is the matrix itself.
nodes.title: First recursive power of a stochastic matrix

nodes.summary: If some power `w` of a stochastic matrix is all-positive, then every later power `m ≥ w` is all-positive: write `m = (m - w) + w`, use `matPow_add`, and note that row `i` of `matPow (m - w)` sums to `1`, so some entry of that row is positive, and that entry times the positive `matPow w` entry gives a positive summand.
nodes.title: Later powers of a positive stochastic matrix power stay positive

nodes.summary: Powers of a power: `(P.pow p).matPow n = P.matPow (p * n)`.
nodes.title: Recursive powers of a stochastic matrix power

nodes.summary: Every row of every power of a stochastic matrix sums to `1`: powers of a stochastic matrix are stochastic.
nodes.title: Powers of a stochastic matrix are stochastic

nodes.summary: The identity chain is not ergodic (for `M ≥ 1`): every power has a zero off-diagonal entry.
nodes.title: The identity Markov chain is not ergodic

nodes.summary: Every positive power of an ergodic chain is ergodic.
nodes.title: Powers of an ergodic Markov chain are ergodic

nodes.summary: The `p`-th power of a stochastic matrix, as a stochastic matrix.
nodes.title: Power of a stochastic matrix

nodes.summary: The identity chain has the displayed transition probabilities.
nodes.title: Transition probabilities of the identity chain

nodes.summary: The uniform chain has constant transition probabilities `1 / (M + 1)`.
nodes.title: Transition probabilities of the uniform chain

nodes.summary: The stationary distribution of a primitive stochastic matrix has full support.
nodes.title: Stationary distribution of a primitive chain has full support

nodes.summary: A primitive stochastic matrix has at most one stationary distribution. In fact `π'` may be any stationary vector of total mass `1`, not necessarily nonnegative.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the stationary distribution of a primitive chain

nodes.summary: For a primitive stochastic matrix with stationary distribution `π`, every row of `Pⁿ` converges to `π`: `Pⁿ(x, y) → π(y)`.
nodes.title: Convergence of matrix powers to the stationary distribution

nodes.summary: The underlying matrix of `P.pow p` is the `p`-th matrix power of `P`.
nodes.title: Underlying matrix of a stochastic matrix power

nodes.summary: Underlying matrix of probabilities of a `StochasticMatrix`.
nodes.title: Underlying matrix of a stochastic matrix

nodes.summary: Doeblin's argument (Levin, Peres and Wilmer, proof of Theorem 4.9): if the `r`-step transition probabilities dominate `δ π`, then the total variation distance of `Pⁿ(x, ·)` from the stationary distribution `π` is at most `(1 - δ) ^ ⌊n / r⌋`. The bound is informative when `r > 0` and `0 < δ`; for `r = 0` (`n / 0 = 0`) or `δ ≤ 0` it reads `d_TV ≤ 1` or weaker.
nodes.title: Doeblin's argument

nodes.summary: The uniform chain: every transition has probability `1 / (M + 1)`.
nodes.title: Uniform Markov chain on finitely many states
